mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4% in the month prior to the prediction is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to reduced risk-free discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the tightening phase (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not cross the 4% threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE exceeding 0.2 percentage points coincides with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days, reflecting reduced labor market tightness and improved investor sentiment.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by >0.2pp in the current month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite UNRATE rising by >0.2pp (p < 0.05), or the effect is not significant in non-loosening regimes.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly index of industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 96.0 for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is predicted to be positive, indicating sustained economic expansion and equity optimism.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive during such expansion windows (p > 0.05), or INDPRO does not sustain the level.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the monthly GDP deflator proxy (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% from the prior month triggers a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return, reflecting expectations of tighter monetary policy and supply-side constraints.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by >0.5% from prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such CPI declines (p > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL does not fall as predicted.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both FEDFUNDS and HOUST (industrial production) by at least 1% over the prior month produce a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return, signaling dual easing in monetary policy and supply chain activity.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < prev and HOUST < prev by ≥1% in the same month
regime_hint: Dual easing in policy and production
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not positive when both triggers are met (p > 0.05), or interaction effect rank IC < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 10,000 monthly over the prior quarter is associated with a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return, reflecting stronger labor market absorption and optimism.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10,000 in the current month relative to the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive during such employment spikes (p > 0.05), or the effect is absent in non-expansion regimes.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly demand indicators RSAFS and GDPC1 both rise simultaneously by at least 2% from the prior month, the S&P 20-day forward return is predicted to be positive, reflecting coordinated economic strength.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by ≥2% and GDPC1 increases by ≥2% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when both proxies meet the threshold (p > 0.05), or interaction effect is not significant.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% for three consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return due to over-supply in the labor market and muted growth expectations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such unemployment lows (p > 0.05), or the regime is not characterized by saturation.
